info.name: Scarlata API (v1)
info.description:
Scarlata - Costa Rica outdoor-spot tracker. Local dev API.

WHAT THIS API IS SHAPED LIKE
- Auth is SESSION COOKIES, not tokens. There is no Authorization header anywhere in this API.
  Run 'Auth > 2. Login' once and Postman carries the cookie automatically for localhost:3001.
  If requests suddenly start returning 401, the session expired (24h) - just log in again.
- Every request that sends a body sends JSON, with Content-Type: application/json.
- Reads are public. Writes to /spots are ADMIN ONLY - users do not create spots.
- Everything under /spots/:id uses {{spotId}}, which 'List all spots' fills in.

VARIABLES
- baseUrl   comes from the 'Scarlata - Local' environment
- spotId    filled in for you by 'List all spots' and 'Create spot', so you should never need
            to paste an id by hand

SUGGESTED FIRST RUN
  1. Auth > 1. Register                 you are now a normal user
  2. Spots - public > List all spots
  3. Error cases > 403                  proves users cannot create spots
  4. Promote yourself to admin          see the 'Create spot' description, then Login again
  5. Spots - admin only > Create spot

Only endpoints that EXIST TODAY are in here. Users interact with spots (status, votes, reviews,
visit logs) and read their own progress under 'My logbook'; admins curate spots and the gallery.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Register / login / logout. Start here - almost everything else needs a session.

request.description:
Creates an account and signs you in immediately - the response sets the session cookie,
so you do not need to call Login right after.

BODY: username, email, password. All three required.
  username  3-30 characters: letters, numbers, dots, dashes, underscores. No @, because
            login accepts a username OR an email and the two must not be confusable.
  email     a valid address, stored lowercased: Ana@x.com and ana@x.com are the same account,
            and login by email works in any case
  password  8-128 characters
Any other key (role, say) is rejected, not ignored.

NEW ACCOUNTS ARE ALWAYS role='user'. There is deliberately no route that grants admin.
See 'Spots - admin only > Create spot' for how to promote yourself.

Success: 201 Created
Errors:  409 if the email or username is already taken
         400 validation, with a details entry per bad field

exec: pm.test("no password hash leaks in the response", () => {

request.description:
Signs in and sets the session cookie. Postman stores cookies per domain automatically, so
every request after this one is authenticated - you do not add any header yourself.

BODY: username + password.
NOTE: the 'username' field also accepts the EMAIL address. The User model passes
usernameQueryFields: ['email'] to passport-local-mongoose, so login matches on either one.

Success: 200 OK
Errors:  401 on wrong credentials

exec: console.log('Signed in as', u.username, '| role:', u.role);

request.description:
Returns the signed-in user. The React client will call this on page load to work out
whether it has a session at all.

NO BODY. Requires the session cookie.

Success: 200 OK
Errors:  401 if signed out

exec: console.log('Signed in as', u.username, '| role:', u.role);

request.description:
Destroys the session.

NO BODY, no headers.

Success: 200 OK

request.description:
Every spot on the map. PUBLIC - works signed out.

NO BODY, NO AUTH, no headers.

ORDER: alphabetical by Spanish rules (accents ignored, n before ñ).

QUERY PARAMS:
  q             text search, Spanish stemming, accent-insensitive: 'rio' finds 'Río', 'cataratas'
                finds 'Catarata'. Ranked by relevance instead of by name. Blank is a 400.
  activityType, province  disabled placeholders for the filtering that lands later.

Success: 200 OK, a JSON array. It will be empty until you run the seed script (npm run seed) or
         create a spot as an admin.

This request saves the first spot's id into {{spotId}}, so the requests below just work.

exec: console.log('No spots yet. Run the seed script (npm run seed), or Create spot as an admin.');

request.description:
One spot by id. PUBLIC.

NO BODY, NO AUTH.

{{spotId}} is filled in automatically by 'List all spots' or 'Create spot'. You can also
set it by hand under the collection's Variables tab.

Success: 200 OK
Errors:  404 if no spot has that id
         400 if the id is not a valid ObjectId shape (24 hex chars)

item.name: Spots - admin only
item.description: Curation. Every request here needs role='admin' - see 'Create spot' for how to get it.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Catarata del Toro",
  "description": "A 90m waterfall dropping into an extinct volcanic crater near Bajos del Toro.",
  "province": "Alajuela",
  "activityTypes": ["waterfall", "hiking"],
  "difficulty": "moderate",
  "bestTimeOfDay": "morning",
  "waterfallHeightM": 90,
  "trailLengthKm": 1.5,
  "estimatedDurationHrs": 2,
  "swimmable": false,
  "oneDayTrip": true,
  "location": {
    "type": "Point",
    "coordinates": [-84.2247, 10.2081]
  }
}

request.description:
Adds a spot to the map. ADMIN ONLY.

HOW TO BECOME AN ADMIN - there is no route for it, on purpose. Register normally, then flip
the field directly in MongoDB:

    mongosh scarlata
    db.users.updateOne({ username: 'samuel' }, { $set: { role: 'admin' } })

Then run 'Auth > 2. Login' again so the session picks up the new role.

BODY - required: name, province, difficulty, activityTypes (at least one), location.coordinates
Also accepted wrapped as { "spot": { ... } }.

  province       one of the seven, spelled WITH ACCENTS exactly as in models/spot.js:
                 San Jose / Alajuela / Cartago / Heredia / Guanacaste / Puntarenas / Limon
                 (copy the accented spellings out of the model - the enum is strict)
  difficulty     easy | moderate | hard
  activityTypes  array. hiking, waterfall, river, camping, viewpoint, hot-springs,
                 hanging-bridges, zipline, rafting, snorkeling
  coordinates    [longitude, latitude] - LONGITUDE FIRST. That is GeoJSON order and it is the
                 reverse of what Google Maps shows you. Costa Rica sits around lng -86 to -82,
                 lat 8 to 11, so the FIRST number should be negative. Anything outside the mainland box is
                 rejected, which is what catches swapped coordinates.
  addedBy        do not send it. The server sets it from your session, and a request that
                 includes it is rejected, so nobody can rewrite who added a spot.
  images         do not send it either. The gallery routes own it.

Everything else (trailLengthKm, waterfallHeightM, maxOccupancy, permitRequired...) is
optional and only applies to some kinds of spot. Numeric specs must be positive
(elevationGainM may be 0), maxOccupancy a whole number. Unknown keys are rejected.

Success: 201 Created
Errors:  401 signed out
         403 signed in but not an admin
         400 validation - the response carries a 'details' object naming each bad field

exec: pm.test("no 'author' field - spots are not user-owned", () =>
console.log("403 - you are signed in but not an admin. Read this request's description.");

request.description:
Edits a spot. ADMIN ONLY.

BODY: send only the fields you want to change - it is a partial update, untouched fields
keep their values. Send null to clear an optional field. At least one field is required,
and the same rules as Create apply to whatever you do send (addedBy and images are
rejected here too).

The route loads the document and calls save(), rather than findByIdAndUpdate, so ALL schema
validators run against the WHOLE document. An invalid enum is rejected even if it sits in a
field you did not send.

Success: 200 OK - returns the updated spot
Errors:  401, 403, 404, or 400 validation

Removes a spot. ADMIN ONLY.

NO BODY.

CASCADES: the post('findOneAndDelete') hook in models/spot.js also deletes every SpotEntry
(someone's toVisit/visited record) and every Review pointing at this spot, so nothing is
left orphaned in the database.

Success: 204 No Content. The response body is EMPTY - that is correct, not a bug. There is
         nothing meaningful to return about a thing that no longer exists.
Errors:  401, 403, 404

item.name: Spots - my activity (signed in)
item.description:
What a signed-in user does with a spot: mark it, then vote on it. Voting needs a visit first.
Status values are 'want' (the to-visit list) and 'visited'. Login first.

request.description:
Puts this spot on your visited list. Creates your entry if none exists, otherwise updates it.

BODY: status = 'want' | 'visited'

Success: 200, your entry
Errors:  401 signed out, 400 bad status, 404 unknown spot

Puts this spot on your to-visit list. Moving it out of 'visited' also clears any vote you cast,
since a vote is only allowed on a visited spot.

Casts (or changes) your vote. One vote per person per spot; posting again replaces it.

BODY: vote = 1 (up) | -1 (down)

Setup: mark the spot visited first.
Success: 200, your entry
Errors:  401 signed out, 403 not visited yet, 400 vote is not 1 or -1, 404 unknown spot
Same as Vote up, with -1.
Clears your vote and leaves the visit itself alone. Tallies on 'Get one spot' (votes.up / votes.down) update.

item.name: Reviews
item.description:
Reviews on a spot. Reading is public; writing needs a visit. One review per person per spot.
Mounted at /spots/:id/reviews.

request.description: PUBLIC. Newest first, author populated with username only.

BODY: rating (1-5), body (max 2000 characters)

Setup: signed in, and the spot marked visited.
Success: 201. Saves the review id into {{reviewId}}.
Errors:  401 signed out, 403 not visited, 409 you already reviewed this spot, 400 validation

Partial update, either field. Only the author can edit (an admin can too, for moderation).
Errors: 401, 403 not yours, 404 review not found under this spot, 400 validation
Author or admin. Success: 204, no body.

item.name: Visit logs
item.description:
Your private record of each trip to a spot, kept on your entry. Only you can see or change your logs.
Everything except the read needs a visit. Mounted at /spots/:id/logs.

item.name: List my logs for this spot

request.description: Your logs for this spot, or an empty array if you have none (including when you have only marked it want).

BODY (all optional)
  visitedAt       ISO date, defaults to now, not in the future
  activitiesDone  list drawn from THIS spot's activityTypes
  notes           free text
  photos          [{ url }], http(s) URLs only until uploads land, at most 10. A
                  client-sent filename is rejected: it will be the Cloudinary id.
Also accepted wrapped as { "log": { ... } }.

Setup: spot marked visited. Saves the log id into {{logId}}.
Success: 201, the new log
Errors:  401, 403 not visited, 400 activity not offered by the spot / bad photo URL / future date
Partial: only the fields you send change, same rules as Add a log, at least one field. Success: 200. Errors: 404 no such log on your entry.
Success: 204.

item.name: Gallery - admin only
item.description: Promoting standout visit-log photos into a spot's curated gallery. Needs role='admin'.

item.name: List user photos for a spot

request.description:
Every photo users attached to their logs for this spot, with the owner. Saves the first entryId
into {{entryId}} so Promote just works (copy the log id and url from the response).

item.name: Promote a photo to the gallery

request.description:
BODY: entryId, logId, url (all from 'List user photos for a spot'). The photo is looked up on the
stored log, and the credit is set to its owner.

Success: 201, the new gallery image
Errors:  403 not admin, 404 no such photo, 409 already in the gallery

Gallery images have no id of their own, so the image is named by url in the query string.
Success: 204. Errors: 403, 404.

item.name: My logbook
item.description: The signed-in user's own view: their lists and their progress. Read-only. Mounted at /me.

request.description: { want: [...], visited: [...] }. Each item: { spot, vote, logs, updatedAt }, most recently touched first.

Visited / total overall, per province and per activity type. A spot with several activities counts
once toward each, so byActivity adds up to more than the overall total.

item.name: Error cases (what good failures look like)
item.description:
Not busywork - these are exactly the behaviours Parts 1 and 1.5 were built to get right.
Run them to see the difference between 401 and 403, and to see validation errors that name
the field that actually failed.

request.description:
SETUP: run 'Auth > 4. Logout' first.

Shows that the API distinguishes 'I do not know who you are' (401) from 'I know you and you
may not do this' (403). The client needs that difference: 401 means show a login screen,
403 means show an error.

SETUP: run Register, or Login as an account whose role is still 'user'.

This is the entire point of the ownership correction. Users explore, visit, vote and review
spots - they do not create them, because a user-submitted spot cannot be verified as a real
and reachable place.

SETUP: must be signed in AS AN ADMIN, otherwise you get 403 before validation ever runs.

Two bad enum values at once. The response names BOTH in a 'details' object keyed by field,
which is the shape react-hook-form wants so it can attach each message to the right input.

Each details entry is { message, type }. The message is developer-facing English; the
type (any.only, any.required, ...) is the stable key the frontend maps to Spanish copy.
This one also flags activityTypes, which is required.

A string that is not a valid ObjectId. Mongoose throws a CastError, which used to fall
through as a 500. Now correctly 400 - the request was bad, the server was fine.

A perfectly valid ObjectId that matches no document. Contrast with the request above:
malformed id = 400, well-formed id that finds nothing = 404.

SETUP: run '1. Register' first so the email exists.

Returns a clean 'That email is already taken'. It deliberately no longer echoes the raw
MongoDB error, which used to leak the database name, collection name and index name straight
to the client. Fixed in utils/normalizeError.js.

item.name: Validation - one bad request per route
item.description:
Each request here sends a body the schemas in server/schemas.js reject, and checks the
field and Joi error type that come back. Validation runs LAST in each route chain, so the
setup matters: signed out you get 401, as a non-admin 403, on an unvisited spot 403.
Run the happy-path folders first so {{spotId}} and {{logId}} are filled in.

Setup per request is in its description.

request.description:
Signed out is fine. Without validation this object reached passport and became a Mongo
$ne query matching the first user. Now it has to be a string.
Signed out is fine. Unknown keys are rejected, so nobody can register themselves as admin.
Signed out is fine. Two fields fail at once; details names both.
SETUP: admin. [lat, lng] instead of [lng, lat] lands outside Costa Rica, and images is owned by the gallery routes.
SETUP: admin. Who added a spot is a record, not an editable field.
SETUP: admin. An update has to change something.
SETUP: signed in. Only 'want' or 'visited'.
SETUP: signed in, spot marked visited. Only 1 or -1.

request.description: SETUP: signed in, spot marked visited. Whole stars only; a body that trims to nothing is empty.
SETUP: signed in as the review author. Only rating and body are editable.
